check_file_size.long_help:
Deprecated: this command has moved to `tingle code_check file_size` and will be removed in a future release. It still works, but prints a warning on stderr.

See: tingle --help code_check

code_check.long_help:
Code evaluation checks, grouped as subcommands.

Usage:
    tingle code_check <subcommand> [options]
    tingle code_check <subcommand> --help

Subcommands:
    file_size    Token efficiency triage: file size analysis.
    rubycritic   Ruby code complexity via RubyCritic (Docker).

The file_size subcommand:

Analyzes source files and lists them by size (line count), classifying them by configurable thresholds. Useful for identifying token consumption bottlenecks before feeding a repository to an AI.

Usage:
    tingle code_check file_size <path> [options]

File selection:
    --exclude a,b                  Extra directory names to skip (comma-separated).
                                   Adds to the defaults (node_modules, dist, build,
                                   .git, ...). Whole path components relative to
                                   <path>, case-insensitive.
    --no-default-excludes          Do not skip the default directories; only
                                   --exclude names apply.
    --no-gitignore                 Do not skip files ignored by git. By default, when
                                   <path> is in a git repository, untracked files
                                   ignored by git (.gitignore, .git/info/exclude,
                                   global excludes) are skipped; tracked files are
                                   always analysed. Without git nothing is skipped.
    --ignore GLOB                  Skip files whose path relative to <path> matches
                                   GLOB (can be repeated). Wins over --include.
    --include GLOB                 Only analyse files whose path relative to <path>
                                   matches GLOB (can be repeated). Combined with
                                   --ext using AND.
                                   Globs ignore case; ** crosses directories, a
                                   pattern without / matches in any directory.

Display:
    --top N                        Show only the N largest files (0 = all).
    --min-level ok|warn|error|critical
                                   Show only files at this level or higher
                                   (default: ok). Applied before --top.
                                   Summary, Total and --fail-on always count
                                   every analysed file.

CI gate:
    --fail-on warn|error|critical  Exit with status 2 if any analysed file reaches
                                   that level or higher (counts every analysed
                                   file, including rows hidden by --top or
                                   --min-level).
                                   The full report is always printed first.

Configuration:
    Defaults for every option can be set in ~/.tingle/code_check/config.json,
    in its "file_size" section (other top-level keys are ignored):

        {"file_size": {"warn": 300, "exclude": ["fixtures"],
                       "gitignore": false, "fail_on": "error"}}

    A legacy "check_file_size" section is still read, with a deprecation
    warning on stderr; setting both sections is an error (exit 1).

    Keys are the flag names with - replaced by _ (warn, error, critical, top,
    exclude, ignore, include, ext, no_default_excludes, fail_on, min_level);
    list keys (exclude, ignore, include, ext) take JSON lists. "gitignore"
    (default true) is the inverse of --no-gitignore. Command-line values win
    for single values; lists from the config and the command line are merged.
    --no-default-excludes and --no-gitignore always win when given.
    --no-config                    Do not read ~/.tingle/code_check/config.json

Exit codes:
    0  Success, or gate passed / not requested
    1  Error: path not found, unknown option, invalid value or invalid
       config file
    2  Size gate failed (--fail-on)

The report goes to stdout and errors go to stderr. Colours are used only when the
output is a terminal and NO_COLOR is unset or empty; otherwise output is plain text.

Examples:
    tingle code_check file_size ./src
    tingle code_check file_size ./src --warn 300 --error 500 --critical 1000
    tingle code_check file_size ./src --top 20
    tingle code_check file_size ./src --min-level warn
    tingle code_check file_size ./src --min-level error --top 5
    tingle code_check file_size ./src --exclude fixtures
    tingle code_check file_size . --no-default-excludes --exclude fixtures
    tingle code_check file_size . --no-gitignore
    tingle code_check file_size ./src --ext .py --ext .js
    tingle code_check file_size ./src --fail-on error
    tingle code_check file_size . --ignore '*.test.js' --ignore 'docs/**'
    tingle code_check file_size . --include 'src/**' --ext .py
    tingle code_check file_size . --no-config

The rubycritic subcommand:

Runs RubyCritic in the darthjee/tingle_rubycritic Docker image on the .rb files
under <path> and measures each file's total Flog complexity, classifying files
by configurable thresholds. Docker is required; the image is pulled when it is
missing. The RubyCritic rating is shown for information only.

Usage:
    tingle code_check rubycritic <path> [options]

    <path> is a Ruby file or a directory (analysed recursively).

File selection:
    --exclude a,b                  Extra directory names to skip (comma-separated).
                                   Adds to the defaults (node_modules, dist, build,
                                   .git, vendor, ..., tmp, log, .bundle). Whole
                                   path components relative to <path>,
                                   case-insensitive.
    --no-default-excludes          Do not skip the default directories; only
                                   --exclude names apply.
    --no-gitignore                 Do not skip files ignored by git. By default,
                                   when <path> is in a git repository, untracked
                                   files ignored by git (.gitignore,
                                   .git/info/exclude, global excludes) are skipped;
                                   tracked files are always analysed. Without git
                                   nothing is skipped.
    --ignore GLOB                  Skip files whose path relative to <path> matches
                                   GLOB (can be repeated). Wins over --include.
    --include GLOB                 Only analyse .rb files whose path relative to
                                   <path> matches GLOB (can be repeated).
                                   Globs ignore case; ** crosses directories, a
                                   pattern without / matches in any directory.

    Symlinks whose target is outside the mounted directory, or missing, are
    skipped silently; a kept symlink is analysed and shown as its target, and
    a symlink and its target count once. Directory symlinks are not walked.
    When <path> is a single file, the directory excludes do not apply and the
    globs match the file name.

Thresholds:
    --warn N                       Warn threshold on the file's total Flog
                                   complexity (default: 100).
    --error N                      Error threshold on the file's total Flog
                                   complexity (default: 200).
    --critical N                   Critical threshold on the file's total Flog
                                   complexity (default: 400).

Display:
    --top N                        Show only the top N most complex files
                                   (default: 0 = all).
    --min-level ok|warn|error|critical
                                   Show only files at this level or higher
                                   (default: ok). Applied before --top.
    --details [N]                  Show the N most complex methods under each
                                   file (default when given without N: 5;
                                   0 = all).

CI gate:
    --fail-on warn|error|critical  Exit with status 2 if any file reaches this
                                   level or higher (counts every analysed file,
                                   including rows hidden by --top or --min-level).
                                   The full report is always printed first.

Image:
    --image IMAGE                  Docker image to run
                                   (default: darthjee/tingle_rubycritic:<tingle version>).

Configuration:
    Defaults for every option can be set in ~/.tingle/code_check/config.json,
    in its "rubycritic" section (other top-level keys are ignored):

        {"rubycritic": {"warn": 50, "exclude": ["db"], "fail_on": "error"}}

    Keys are the flag names with - replaced by _ (warn, error, critical, top,
    exclude, ignore, include, no_default_excludes, fail_on, min_level, image,
    details); list keys (exclude, ignore, include) take JSON lists. "gitignore"
    (default true) is the inverse of --no-gitignore. There is no "ext" key.
    Command-line values win for single values; lists from the config and the
    command line are merged. --no-default-excludes and --no-gitignore always
    win when given.
    --no-config                    Do not read ~/.tingle/code_check/config.json

Exit codes:
    0  Success, gate passed / not requested, or no Ruby files found
    1  Error: path not found, unknown option, invalid value, invalid config
       file, Docker not found or not running, image pull failed, or the
       container failed
    2  Complexity gate failed (--fail-on)

The report goes to stdout and errors go to stderr. Colours are used only when the
output is a terminal and NO_COLOR is unset or empty; otherwise output is plain text.

Examples:
    tingle code_check rubycritic ./app
    tingle code_check rubycritic ./app --warn 50 --error 100 --critical 200
    tingle code_check rubycritic ./app --top 10
    tingle code_check rubycritic ./app --min-level warn
    tingle code_check rubycritic ./app --fail-on error
    tingle code_check rubycritic ./app --exclude fixtures
    tingle code_check rubycritic . --no-default-excludes --exclude fixtures
    tingle code_check rubycritic . --no-gitignore
    tingle code_check rubycritic . --ignore 'spec/**' --ignore '*_spec.rb'
    tingle code_check rubycritic . --include 'app/**' --include 'lib/**'
    tingle code_check rubycritic ./app --image tingle_rubycritic:dev
    tingle code_check rubycritic . --no-config

kube.short_help: Kubernetes (EKS) subcommand with a scoped alias layer.
kube.long_help:
Kubernetes (EKS) helper built around short, scoped aliases for contexts, namespaces, and pods, backed by ~/.tingle/kube/config.json. Reads and validates that config (schema: version, aws_profile, pod_id_pattern, shell, contexts, namespaces, pods), applying defaults (aws_profile: default, pod_id_pattern: ^[a-z0-9]{10}$, shell: bash) when fields are absent, and degrades gracefully to pass-through mode when the config is missing or invalid.

`configure context|namespace|pod` runs an interactive prompt-only flow to create, edit, or remove aliases at each level (never invokes kubectl/kubectx/aws): `configure context` prompts alias → real name/ARN directly; `configure namespace`/`configure pod` cascade scope (context) → alias → real value, since both live inside a context block. Removing a context alias cascades to delete its namespaces/pods blocks too. Every write is validated against the config schema before saving, so a bad interactive session never corrupts config.json.

Usage:
    tingle kube switch <context_alias>
    tingle kube list [--json] namespace
    tingle kube list [--json] pods
    tingle kube shell <namespace_alias> <pod_alias>
    tingle kube configure context
    tingle kube configure namespace
    tingle kube configure pod

Examples:
    tingle kube switch prod
    tingle kube list namespace
    tingle kube list --json namespace
    tingle kube list --json pods
    tingle kube shell web api
    tingle kube configure context
    tingle kube configure namespace
    tingle kube configure pod
